newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-O'Halloran magic seals win for Hurricanes.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-O'Halloran magic seals win for Hurricanes.

text.p: WELLINGTON, April 28 - Wellington Hurricanes man-for-all-occasions Jason O'Halloran thought his team was staring defeat in the face halfway through the second half of Saturday's Super 12 rugby match against Otago at Athletic Park.
Then he produced his piece of magic -- and not for the first time this season, NZPA reports.
The Hurricanes, 41-3 up after 14 minutes of the second half but battling with a series of injuries, conceded tries in the 16th, 18th, 26th and 31st minutes of the half as Otago switched on.

In fact in those 15 minutes Hurricanes players touched the ball just three times, and just as rapidly lost it. One was turned over, a second kicked away by replacement centre Mark Ranby. Things were becoming desperate, said O'Halloran.
"I thought we were going to get rolled halfway through the half," he said.
"At 10 minutes to go and just 11 points up I felt the best we could do was to hold on and keep them out as long as possible before the next try.
"I thought then that we might manage to sneak in by four points. I was more than certain they were at least going to get another one."

But after those 15 minutes of hectic chasing and tackling, the Hurricanes finally managed to secure scrum possession on the Otago 22. The ball went left from a ruck, going nowhere, and O'Halloran called for the ball.

"I didn't feel anything was on to the left so I called Marty (Leslie) to give the ball to me behind the ruck. I skirted to the right and we had a three-to-two advantage there. I feinted to put one over the top, and my guy sat back a bit.
"I think it was a flanker -- luckily it was a forward, so I scooted around him and under the bar."
It wasn't the first time this season O'Halloran has pulled the rug from under an opposition's feet.
Two further tries were added by the Hurricanes against flimsy Otago defence -- making 14 for the match -- to make the final margin a little flattering.

The five points from the win has given the side a fine semifinal chance, despite crippling injuries to centre Alama Ieremia, who has a broken collarbone, and No 8 Karl Williams, who tore a groin muscle.

The match, before 35,000 spectators, was notable for fine individual performances by O'Halloran, Tana Umaga, Alex Telea and Stephen Bachop in the backs, but the forwards became disrupted by injury and could not establish a set piece platform in the second half.
Umaga was superb with his three tries. He is really pushing his case for further recognition by a national panel which has so far refused to acknowledge his class.
But this is a different Umaga this season, who cannot be ignored.
"It's what we've come to expect from him. They (the All Black selectors) have to be looking at him now. I can't see a better winger in the competition."
Taine Randell and Josh Kronfeld had big moments in the Otago forwards and fullback Matthew Carrington is a classy mover.
